qa.a: We cannot say yet. Collection began on 14 Nov 2026 and that is the only day so far (190,220 for sale, 34,248 to rent). December's pack will show the first change.
qa.q: Did stock rise or fall in November?

qa.a: Leaning seller's: only 2.7% of 2,129 sampled sale listings are price-reduced (vs a ~20% buyer's-market line) and offers pending (6.9%) outnumber cuts 2.6 to 1. One day of data.
qa.q: Is this a buyer's or seller's market?

qa.a: West Rand (15.8% gross 2-bed yield), East Rand (14.5%) and Johannesburg (10.8%) clear the 10.5% bond rate; Cape Town (4.8%) and the Garden Route (4.3%) do not.
qa.q: Where should a buy-to-let investor look?

qa.a: Partly: 'houses for sale' searches are 8% below last November (80.5 vs 87.3) and 'flats to rent' 25% lower (13.5 vs 18.0), but January is the seasonal peak (95).
Cape Town: 69.5 in November and steady at 66.8-72.3 since June. Johannesburg is weakest, down 16% since June to 39.0 despite the most stock (28,027).
qa.q: Which metro has the strongest buyer interest?

qa.a: Pam Golding and RE/MAX at 10.2% each of 4,394 sampled listings; in the biggest regions the leaders are Rawson (Johannesburg), Century 21 (East Rand), Homii (Durban), Just Property (Pretoria) and RE/MAX (Cape Town).

c1.sql: SELECT province "Province", sum(listings) FILTER (WHERE deal_type='sale') "Homes for sale", sum(listings) FILTER (WHERE deal_type='rent') "Homes to rent", round(100.0*sum(listings) FILTER (WHERE deal_type='sale')/sum(sum(listings) FILTER (WHERE deal_type='sale')) OVER (),1) "Share of sale stock %", round(sum(listings) FILTER (WHERE deal_type='sale')::numeric/sum(listings) FILTER (WHERE deal_type='rent'),1) "Sale-to-rent ratio" FROM analyst.property_stock WHERE day='2026-11-14' AND is_province_total AND category='residential' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

steps: Stock (sections 1, 5): analyst.property_stock, Private Property, day 14 Nov 2026 only (the one collected day in 1-30 Nov 2026); province totals and 48 regions kept separate; residential sale/rent plus commercial province totals.

Prices, yields, flags, agencies (sections 2, 3, 6): analyst.property_listings sample seen 14 Nov 2026 (2,129 residential sale, 2,265 rent); medians via percentile_cont(0.5), NULL prices excluded; 2-bed yield = 12 x median rent / median asking, sectional types, min 5 listings each side; bond rate from analyst.bond_rate (10.5%, 14 Nov 2026).
Change tables: property_stock_changes has no previous day (14 Nov is the baseline); property_daily_activity is empty and Property24 rows are absent, so new-listing flow uses the is_new flag.

Demand (section 4): analyst.search_interest groups 'property: buying vs renting · 12 months' and 'property: metros · 12 months', monthly averages of weekly values Jun-Nov 2026 (Nov = weeks of 1 and 8 Nov); year-ago and January comparisons from the same pull (Nov 2025-Nov 2026).
trust: Stock counts are complete portal counts, not samples.
Search-interest comparisons stay within one term group and pull, as the index requires.
Price-cut and yield directions are consistent across the large regions (~60 sale listings each).
limits: No listing, stock or bond-rate data before 14 Nov 2026: no earlier-month figures and no within-month trend in this edition.
Sample medians lean to featured/newer listings; regional 2-bed sale samples are 5-22 listings, so yields are indicative asking-price yields.
Property24 not yet collected; portal counts are never added, and 'not stated' agency is not confirmed private sellers.

risks: One collection day: every figure is a snapshot, and within-month change could not be measured.
Medians, yields, flags and agency shares come from a first-pages sample (featured/newer first); several yields rest on 5 sale listings.
Asking prices are not sale prices; gross yields exclude levies, rates, vacancy and costs.
Google Trends is relative and November holds two weekly points; the portal's 10.5% bond rate may differ from banks' posted prime.
actions: 1. Publish week-on-week stock change from the next collection days in December, and load Property24 newest listings to measure new-mandate flow and share.
2. Agencies: canvass December mandates in Johannesburg, Pretoria and Durban so stock is live and photographed before the January search peak (95 last year).
3. Prospect re-pricing mandates on the Garden Route and Dolphin Coast, where cut rates (9.1%, 7.4%) are about 3x the 2.7% national level.
4. Investors: shortlist 2-bed sectional stock in the West Rand (R599k median) and East Rand (R579k); verify Nelson Mandela Bay and Amatola with bigger samples first.
5. Developers: avoid sale-only product in sale-heavy coastal regions (KZN South Coast 20.8, West Coast 20.5 for sale per rental); test rental product instead.
6. Franchise principals: add 10-15 front-page mandates in a big region; leaders hold only 9-15 listings in their region's sample.
findings: Baseline 14 Nov 2026: 190,220 homes for sale and 34,248 to rent; Gauteng holds 44% of sale stock and five regions hold 50%.
Pricing pressure is low: 2.7% of sampled sale listings price-reduced, 6.9% offer pending; cuts cluster on the Garden Route (9.1%) and Dolphin Coast (7.4%).
National 2-bed gross yield (10.1%) sits just under the 10.5% bond rate; 11 of 20 regions clear it, led by West Rand (15.8%) and East Rand (14.5%); Cape Town 4.8%.
Search demand peaked in July (86.8), troughed in September (77.8) and is 8% below last November; January is the seasonal high (95).
Johannesburg pairs the largest stock (28,027) with falling search interest (-16% since June): the clearest supply-demand mismatch.
Metro agency share is fragmented: each top-5 region has a different leader, none above 27.3% of branded listings.
